lede: The biggest thing to watch this week is the TMVOA Board of Directors kicking off its three-meeting 2027 budget cycle on Thursday, November 6 — they'll be reviewing the completed 2025 audit and getting a first look at next year's draft budget, so this is the moment to start paying attention if Mountain Village assessments or services affect you. The regional intergovernmental meeting on Sunday, November 9, brings Telluride, Mountain Village, Ophir, Norwood, and the county together for a cross-jurisdictional large-projects update — the kind of session where things that matter to the whole valley get aired quietly. On the lighter side, the week has plenty going on, from the Adult Spelling Bee Friday night to the Wildbelly Fermentation Fest Saturday and a Free Legal Clinic Tuesday.

notable.stake: Height variance and easement quasi-judicial reviews could set precedent for Mountain Village property disputes.
First look at TMVOA 2027 draft budget and 2025 audit affects every Mountain Village owner's assessments.
Regional large-projects update surfaces cross-jurisdictional development and infrastructure pressures affecting the whole valley.
